prompt: An L-shape has outer dimensions $6 \times 4$. The inner cut is $2 \times 2$. Find the perimeter.
hint: Perimeter is the distance around the outside, not the space inside. Cutting a corner removes two short edges and adds two new ones.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Start with the plain $6 \times 4$ rectangle with no cut. Its perimeter is $2(6 + 4) = 20$. Then ask what the corner cut changes.
Perimeter is the distance around the outside, not the space inside. Cutting a corner removes two short edges and adds two new ones.
The cut removes $2$ from one side and $2$ from another, then adds two inner edges of $2$ each. List the six sides: $6$, $4$, $4$, $2$, $2$, $2$.
$6 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 20$, so the perimeter of the L-shape is $20$ units.

explanation: Walk around the L-shape and list each edge. The two uncut sides are $6$ and $4$.
The two sides that lost a corner are shorter by $2$: they are $6 - 2 = 4$ and $4 - 2 = 2$.
The cut itself adds two inner edges, each of length $2$.
Add all six edges to get the distance around: $6 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 20$.
The perimeter is $20$ units, the same as the uncut $6 \times 4$ rectangle, because the inner edges replace the missing outer ones.
